    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>

  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the festivals are set according to harvest times, referring to spiritual harvest, and that Sukkos follows the spiritual gathering of produce, raising questions about the connection between the Sukkah and the harvest, and the wording of the verses.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And the Festival of the Harvest... when you gather in your labors from the field."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Baal HaHilula explains,</t>
    <t s="2">that the fact that the festivals are set during the times of the harvest</t>
    <t s="3">is intended</t>
    <t s="4">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="5">for spiritual harvest.</t>
    <t s="6">And this is why the Festival of Sukkos was set at the time of the gathering of the harvest,</t>
    <t s="7">to the point that it is called by the name "Chag HaAsif" (Festival of the Ingathering),</t>
    <t s="8">because the concept of the Festival of Sukkos is connected and comes after the work of gathering the harvest</t>
    <t s="9">("and you shall gather"</t>
    <t s="10">your grain, your wine, and your oil)</t>
    <t s="11">in spirituality.</t>
    <t s="12">And just as the gathering of the harvest in its simple, physical sense is before the onset of the festival,</t>
    <t s="13">for on Yom Tov it is forbidden [to do such work],</t>
    <t s="14">so too in spirituality,</t>
    <t s="15">that after the work of "when you gather the produce of the land"</t>
    <t s="16">(then)</t>
    <t s="17">"you shall celebrate the festival of the L-rd for seven days."</t>
    <t s="18">And one must understand the connection of the Festival of Sukkos,</t>
    <t s="19">whose name</t>
    <t s="20">(Sukkos)</t>
    <t s="21">is from "in Sukkos"</t>
    <t s="22">"you shall dwell for seven days,"</t>
    <t s="23">to "when you gather the produce of the land."</t>
    <t s="24">And one must also understand</t>
    <t s="25">(as is precise in several discourses)</t>
    <t s="26">what is said:</t>
    <t s="27">"In Sukkos you shall dwell for seven days; every citizen of Israel shall dwell in Sukkos,"</t>
    <t s="28">for at first glance,</t>
    <t s="29">the commandment "In Sukkos you shall dwell..." is for the entirety of Israel and for every individual Jew,</t>
    <t s="30">so what is added by saying "every citizen of Israel shall dwell in Sukkos"?</t>
    <t s="31">And one must also understand</t>
    <t s="32">why in the commandment "In Sukkos you shall dwell" it says "you shall dwell for seven days," whereas in the commandment "every citizen..." it says "shall dwell" without specification</t>
    <t s="33">(and does not say "for seven days").</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the connection of the Four Species to the first day of the Festival of Ingathering, noting that while the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah applies all seven days, the mitzvah of the Four Species begins on the first day.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, following "you shall celebrate the festival of the L-rd for seven days," the verse continues:</t>
    <t s="1">"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, a branch of a thick-leaved tree, and willows of the brook..."</t>
    <t s="2">For this mitzvah is also connected to the Festival of the Ingathering,</t>
    <t s="3">for the time of this mitzvah is specifically on the first day,</t>
    <t s="4">on the first day of the festival that comes about because of "when you gather."</t>
    <t s="5">And although the mitzvah of taking the Four Species is not as connected to the essence of the festival as the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah</t>
    <t s="6">[as is also understood from the fact that the obligation of the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah applies throughout all seven days of the festival</t>
    <t s="7">("In Sukkos you shall dwell for seven days"),</t>
    <t s="8">from the time the festival becomes holy,</t>
    <t s="9">whereas the obligation of the mitzvah of taking the Four Species begins in the morning</t>
    <t s="10">(at dawn,</t>
    <t s="11">and ideally at sunrise)</t>
    <t s="12">and only on the first day],</t>
    <t s="13">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="14">this mitzvah is also connected</t>
    <t s="15">(as above)</t>
    <t s="16">with the first day of the Festival of the Ingathering.</t>
  </section>

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Night of the 13th of Tishrei
(the yahrtzeit of the Admo"r Mahara"sh, his soul in Eden),
the year 5743.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the festivals are set according to harvest times, referring to spiritual harvest, and that Sukkos follows the spiritual gathering of produce, raising questions about the connection between the Sukkah and the harvest, and the wording of the verses.

translations.translation: "And the Festival of the Harvest... when you gather in your labors from the field."
And the Baal HaHilula explains,
that the fact that the festivals are set during the times of the harvest
is intended
(primarily)
for spiritual harvest.
And this is why the Festival of Sukkos was set at the time of the gathering of the harvest,
to the point that it is called by the name "Chag HaAsif" (Festival of the Ingathering),
because the concept of the Festival of Sukkos is connected and comes after the work of gathering the harvest
("and you shall gather"
your grain, your wine, and your oil)
in spirituality.
And just as the gathering of the harvest in its simple, physical sense is before the onset of the festival,
for on Yom Tov it is forbidden [to do such work],
so too in spirituality,
that after the work of "when you gather the produce of the land"
(then)
"you shall celebrate the festival of the L-rd for seven days."
And one must understand the connection of the Festival of Sukkos,
whose name
(Sukkos)
is from "in Sukkos"
"you shall dwell for seven days,"
to "when you gather the produce of the land."
And one must also understand
(as is precise in several discourses)
what is said:
"In Sukkos you shall dwell for seven days; every citizen of Israel shall dwell in Sukkos,"
for at first glance,
the commandment "In Sukkos you shall dwell..." is for the entirety of Israel and for every individual Jew,
so what is added by saying "every citizen of Israel shall dwell in Sukkos"?
And one must also understand
why in the commandment "In Sukkos you shall dwell" it says "you shall dwell for seven days," whereas in the commandment "every citizen..." it says "shall dwell" without specification
(and does not say "for seven days").

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the connection of the Four Species to the first day of the Festival of Ingathering, noting that while the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah applies all seven days, the mitzvah of the Four Species begins on the first day.

translations.translation: Now, following "you shall celebrate the festival of the L-rd for seven days," the verse continues:
"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, a branch of a thick-leaved tree, and willows of the brook..."
For this mitzvah is also connected to the Festival of the Ingathering,
for the time of this mitzvah is specifically on the first day,
on the first day of the festival that comes about because of "when you gather."
And although the mitzvah of taking the Four Species is not as connected to the essence of the festival as the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah
[as is also understood from the fact that the obligation of the mitzvah of dwelling in the Sukkah applies throughout all seven days of the festival
("In Sukkos you shall dwell for seven days"),
from the time the festival becomes holy,
whereas the obligation of the mitzvah of taking the Four Species begins in the morning
(at dawn,
and ideally at sunrise)
and only on the first day],
nevertheless,
this mitzvah is also connected
(as above)
with the first day of the Festival of the Ingathering.
